PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-06-06
41M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling well overall and takes his blood pressure medication each morning, checking home readings twice a week. Denies chest pain. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks and takeout, which was discussed. He works as a sales representative with frequent driving and irregular meals. Appetite is good and sleep is about 7 hours most nights. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 192 lb, BMI 28.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.1%, fasting glucose 108 mg/dL, lipid panel within goal, basic metabolic panel normal.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 124/78. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks, packing meals for the road, and adding short walks during breaks. Recheck A1c in 6 months with a goal of modest weight loss.
3. Health maintenance: colorectal screening discussed for his age; influenza vaccine offered in the fall. Encouraged regular physical activity and hydration on the road.
4. Lifestyle: reviewed healthier choices during long drives and the importance of regular breaks and consistent sleep.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
